nodes.label: User or calling system
nodes.summary: Submits a task and watches progress; may cancel.

nodes.label: Human approver
nodes.summary: Reviews and approves or denies risky tool calls. MCP says there should always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.

nodes.label: LLM service
nodes.summary: Chooses the next step from the history and the tool descriptions. See note 22 for serving.

nodes.label: Tool servers (MCP or internal APIs)
nodes.summary: Expose tools to the host over a stateful JSON-RPC session; can be local processes or remote services. They must validate inputs, apply access control, rate limit and sanitise outputs.

nodes.label: Session API
nodes.summary: Accepts tasks, streams progress, handles cancel, approvals and trace fetch. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.summary: Runs the agent loop for each run: ask the model, call tools, observe, repeat until done or stopped. Persists each step so another worker can resume.

nodes.label: Agent loop
nodes.summary: LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop; ReAct interleaves reasoning, action and observation.

nodes.label: Budget and stop guard
nodes.summary: Caps steps, tokens, time and money, and detects repeated identical actions. Anthropic notes stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations; ReAct documents repetition loops. The exact guard is our design.

nodes.label: Tool gateway
nodes.summary: Single place to authenticate tools, use the end user's delegated credentials, enforce schemas, timeouts and rate limits, and log calls. Speaks MCP to tool servers.

nodes.label: Sandbox pool
nodes.summary: Isolated, short-lived environments where model-written code or commands run: no platform secrets, restricted network, resource limits. Firecracker documents the isolation technology (KVM micro-VMs, under 5 MB overhead, boot under 125 ms); the agent-specific policy is our design. Anthropic recommends extensive testing in sandboxed environments.

nodes.label: Run state store
nodes.summary: Messages, tool results and checkpoints per run, so a crashed run resumes from its last step. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Approval service
nodes.summary: Holds a pending risky action until a human approves or denies it. Anthropic notes agents can pause for human feedback at checkpoints.

nodes.label: Trace store
nodes.summary: Every model call, tool call, result, cost and latency for each run; replayable for debugging and evaluation. MCP clients should log tool use for audit.

nodes.label: Evaluation harness
nodes.summary: Runs a task suite with automatic success checks (tests for coding) before models, prompts or tools change. Anthropic stresses measuring performance and iterating.

nodes.label: Alternative: fixed workflow
nodes.summary: When the steps are known, use prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers or evaluator-optimizer instead of a free-running agent: more predictable and cheaper.

steps.caption: The task arrives at the session API.
The orchestrator starts the agent loop.
The model gets the history and the available tool descriptions and chooses an action.
The loop sends the chosen tool call to the tool gateway.
If the tool runs code, it executes in a sandbox.
The result is added to the history and the step is checkpointed.
The step is logged to the trace store.
Progress is streamed to the user; the loop repeats until the model finishes.
Each completed step was checkpointed before the crash.
Another worker resumes the run from the last checkpoint.
A tool call that may have executed before the crash is retried; idempotent tools or stored results prevent a repeated side effect (our design reasoning).
The model keeps proposing the same thought and action; ReAct documents this repetition pattern.
The guard sees the step cap, budget or repetition and stops the run.
The user is told why the run stopped and what was done.
The model proposes an irreversible action such as sending money; the loop pauses and asks for approval.
A person sees the exact tool and inputs and decides.
If approved, the call proceeds through the tool gateway; if denied, the denial is returned to the model as the result.

flows.name: A tool result contains injected instructions (failure)

steps.caption: A tool returns text that tries to instruct the agent.
The text enters the model's context as data. Narrow permissions limit what it can do.
A sensitive action it provokes still needs human approval (our design reasoning).
